主要内容: On July 23, 2014, the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) adopted amendments to the rules governing money market mutual funds. The reforms aim to address run risks while preserving the benefits of these funds. The new rules require institutional prime money market funds to use a floating net asset value (NAV), allowing daily share prices to fluctuate with market conditions. Additionally, the rules introduce liquidity fees and redemption gates to manage periods of stress. The reforms also include enhanced diversification, disclosure, and stress testing requirements. A two-year transition period is provided for funds and investors to adjust. The SEC also proposed exemptions from certain confirmation requirements and re-proposed amendments to address credit rating references under the Dodd-Frank Act. The rules will take effect 60 days after publication in the Federal Register. The SEC introduced new tools, such as fees and gates, to address potential liquidity crises by allowing fund boards to impose liquidity fees or temporarily suspend redemptions if liquidity levels fall below a threshold. Additionally, the reforms include enhanced diversification, disclosure, and stress testing requirements, as well as updated reporting standards for funds operating similarly to money market funds. The U.S. Treasury and IRS will release tax guidance to support the implementation of these rules, including a simplified tax accounting method and relief from wash sale rules for floating NAV funds. These reforms follow the 2010 amendments, which aimed to improve the resilience of money market funds after the 2008 financial crisis, and are part of ongoing efforts to address potential risks in the financial system.
